title: नेपालको भाषा नीति Nepalko Bhasha Niti
authors: गिरी Giri, जीवेन्द्र Jibendra देव Dev
nepali: प्रस्तुत अध्ययनमा नेपाल बहुभाषिक देश हो भन्ने कुरा नेपालका भाषाहरूको पारिवारिक वर्गीकरण सहित तथ्यहरूद्वारा स्पष्ट पार्दै नेपालले अङ्गीकार गरेको भाषिक नीतिमा प्रकाश पारिएको छ । यस क्रममा विगतमा अँगालिएको एक भाषिक नीतिबाट विभिन्न भाषाभाषीमा परेको प्रभावबारे जानकारी दिइएको छ र वर्तमान नेपालमा नेपालका सबै भाषाप्रति समान दृष्टिकोण राखिएको तथा विभिन्न भाषाको संरचनागतएवम् स्तरगत विकासका निम्ति विभिन्न कार्य गरिएको र भविष्यमा त्यसले अझ मूर्त रूप प्राप्त गर्दै जाने निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । यस निम्ति सरकारद्वारा उपयुक्त भाषानीति लागू गरिने र जनस्तरको जागरणले त्यसलाई बल पु¥याउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ ।
american_english: In this study, the fact that Nepal is a multilingual country is made clear by means of facts that include the family-wise classification of Nepal's languages, and light is shed on the language policy that Nepal has adopted. In this process, information is given about the impact that the one-language policy of the past had on speakers of different languages, and the conclusion is drawn that in present-day Nepal an equal attitude is held toward all of Nepal's languages and that various works have been carried out for the structural and level-based development of the different languages, which will take an even more concrete form in the future. For this, it is expected that the government will implement a suitable language policy and that public awareness will give it strength.
british_english: In the present study, the fact that Nepal is a multilingual country is made clear by evidence including the genealogical classification of Nepal's languages, and light is thrown on the language policy adopted by Nepal. In this connection, information is provided about the effects that the monolingual policy imposed in the past had on speakers of various languages, and it is concluded that in present-day Nepal an equal attitude is maintained toward all the languages of Nepal and that various measures have been undertaken for the structural and level-wise development of the different languages, which will acquire an even more concrete form in the future. To that end, it is hoped that the government will put in place a suitable language policy and that public awareness will lend it force.
australian_english: In this study, the fact that Nepal is a multilingual country is made clear through facts that include the language-family classification of Nepal's languages, and light is shed on the language policy Nepal has adopted. In this process, information is given about the effect the one-language policy of the past had on speakers of different languages, and the conclusion is reached that in present-day Nepal all of the country's languages are viewed equally and that various works have been done for the structural and level-by-level development of the different languages, and that in the future this will take an even more concrete shape. For this, it is expected that the government will bring in a suitable language policy and that community awareness will give it strength.
informal_english: This study makes it clear that Nepal is a multilingual country, backing it up with facts like how Nepal's languages are sorted into families, and it shines a light on the language policy Nepal has adopted. Along the way, it tells us how the one-language policy of the past affected speakers of different languages, and it concludes that today's Nepal treats all its languages equally and that a bunch of work has been done to develop the different languages structurally and at different levels, which will get even more concrete down the road. The hope is that the government will put a proper language policy in place and that public awareness will give it some muscle.
